utterances.text: Yes. (4.00 pm) (Short break) (4.30 pm) (Witness re-enters court) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Kindly remind him he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I am reminding you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I realise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Welcome back, Mr. Dordic. We were in the process of making a map and it's still sitting next to you. I think where we had got to, if I can get the map up on the screen here, is you had put a "DB" where Dusko Bendjo was sitting at the time we were talking about; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described for us this morning an incident involving another burning, and that person's name is Nedjelko Draganic. Can you show us where he was sitting by marking it with an "ND", please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, you have done that. You have placed an "ND" on what the Registrar has identified as exhibit 11-4, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The next person who I'd like -- whose location I would like you to identify for me is named Momir Kuljanin. Put an "MK".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, you have put an "MK" where Momir Kuljanin was seated; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last one whom I would like you to identify the location of is Milivoj Gligorevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, you have done that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you told us during your direct examination that there was a time when another person was asked to hit Milivoj Gligorevic with a shoe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us again the name of the person -- who it was that was asked to hit him with the shoe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Boro Koprivica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us then on the diagram, by using "BK", where he sat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have done that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the initials "BK"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll now ask the usher to show you what turns out to be an awfully poor photograph, but I think you may be able to identify it, and I want you to tell me if you can. Please put it on the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Have we seen this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Numerous times it has been shown before in the court. Show it to Mr. Turone, just so he knows he has seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. THE USHER: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The one that I'm looking at right now. My only question is: do you recognise that scene? Do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It reminds me of Hangar Number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it show the way that the prisoners were seated in Hangar Number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What that shows is that there were in addition to a row of prisoners against the long walls, there was another row sitting directly in front of that row, so that there would have been four rows lengthwise in that building; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you will now pick that exhibit up off the ELMO, so you can see the diagram you drew, then I'll ask you an additional question. You've got a mark on that diagram that appears to be sitting out in the middle of the floor. I think that's Momir Kuljanin or Nedjelko Draganic. It's Nedjelko Draganic. That mark sitting out in the middle of the floor away from the wall would show that he was really sitting in one of those long rows of people; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: People in those rows along the wall and in front of them were sitting quite close together, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The row that can be seen here, against this wall, and these were -- they were a bit further back. This side here was a bit further back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At this point I will move to introduce the diagram that the witness made that was furnished by the prosecution to us as exhibit 11/4. Then I would also ask that the photograph that I just showed him be marked as an exhibit and I'll move to introduce that when we have a designation for it. Then I also want to move the introduction of the two colour photographs that he identified, which have been marked as Exhibit 5/2 and 6/2?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We have in objection, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Can I have a look at the photograph of Hangar Number 6? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The black and white one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do we have a number assigned now to the photograph that was just handed to Judge Jan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Hocking, take this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's number D12/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then my offer would include D12/4 and the Office of the Prosecutor has already said they have no objection, so I assume that those four that I have offered are now admitted; is that correct? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Since it's not been objected to, they are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I think I have one more area, Mr. Dordic, that I want to discuss with you. I want to remind you of your testimony regarding an incident where Mr. Delic came to Hangar Number 6 and a weapon was fired into the ceiling, and three or four people were injured as a result of the bullet fragmenting and flying around. You remember what I'm talking about; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my recollection of your testimony, although I'm not certain, and that's why I want to ask you about it, is that that happened some time during the month of August 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in August. Some time in July, early July, I believe, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that happened and it became apparent that people were injured, you've told us that Mr. Delic immediately put them in his car and drove them off to Building 22 for treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if it was a car, because I was not outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know that he did take them there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took them somewhere and when they came back, they said that these fragments of the bullets were taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At the time this happened the persons with Mr. Delic were maybe some other guards from Celebici, but no-one else; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That concludes my cross-examination, your Honours. Thank you. Cross-examination by MR. GREAVES

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dordic. May it please your Honours? I would like to ask you, Mr. Dordic, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you just a little bit more about the incident when you were taken by the police to go and recover your weapon that you had hidden. Essentially that was an operation organised by MUP, Jasmin Guska and Sevko Niksic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those two that I've named to you, did they go with you to where the weapon was hidden, or did they send someone to do it for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They sent someone else, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken there in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a Golf vehicle. It was white and blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A Volkswagen Golf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Volkswagen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of the people that took you to that place -- I think name was Sljivo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Sljivo a first or a second name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a last name. I don't recall the first name. I only know that he was a goalkeeper of the soccer club Igman from Konjic and just before the war he was the trainer for the goalkeepers. He was one of the reserve policemen. I don't know if he was a commander there or not but he was in the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask about his function in the police but would the name Dzevad Sljivo, would that sound right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's exactly the name maybe. I only know him as Sljivo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly we may well hear in due course about a reserve police officer by that very name. He was the one who drove the vehicle, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I think it was Vahid Macic who drove -- no, Alagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think when you got to the place where the weapon was concealed, I think you were beaten up by this man Sljivo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He started beating me, but he was warned by this Vahid Alagic and then he stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not to do it in front of your mother; I think was what happened; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I just want briefly to ask you about another man, please, Mr. Dordic, if I may: Jovan Divijak. I am sorry if I mispronounced the name, but does that name ring a bell to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that someone who came at least once to the camp at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him, but he was seen by a prisoner Radovan Mrsic, who knew him personally, like I did, because for a while he was a commander. Jovan Divijak was Commander for the Territorial Defence for Mostar, for the Mostar region, and he spent a lot of time in the training centre in Borci conducting some courses, and if there were these courses going on, I would be there as a cook. So I knew him well. We spent at least one year conducting these courses and these trainings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a Serb or a Muslim or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb. He is a Muslim general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the visit to the camp was about? Were you told that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you told about his visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radovan Mrsic told me -- he said -- I was called "Mrkela". He said: "Mrkela, your friend is coming. He told you -- he told me when he saw me -- he said: 'That's what you deserved'". That's what he said when he saw Radovan Mrsic, because Radovan Mrsic was cleaning something outside at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would your Honour just give me a moment, please? I just want to ask you one question, please, about your interrogation before you actually arrived at the camp. Was one of the people engaged in that process a man called Mensur Kovac? Does that ring a bell, Mr. Dordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mensur Kovac, no, not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see that person at all at the time before the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't even know him. I don't even know who he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never mentioned him anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now just to turn, please, to Mr. Mucic and some details concerning him, please, if we may. You've told their Honours about the first time that you saw him. Would you accept this, please, Mr. Dordic, that, as far as the time when you first saw him, you are not sure in which month it was that you first saw Mr. Mucic in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most probably it was June, the first time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're not sure which month it was, Mr. Dordic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it's correct that I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as his uniform was concerned, it's right, isn't it, that there was no insignia on that uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he did not have insignia. I'm not sure but I think he did not have them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want now to explore something that you told the court earlier on today and the phrase that you used in evidence about Mr. Mucic was that everybody respected him. So I'm just going to ask you a series of questions about that, Mr. Dordic, if I may, please. You obviously knew him before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Without moustache. I'm a waiter and he used to -- he liked to frequent cafes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, nothing wrong with that, is there, if you are a waiter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he -- whereabouts were you employed at that stage? What was the name of the cafe that you worked in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many different cafes. I don't want to list them. At least ten that I worked in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which was the one that he used to come to and drink at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he would come to all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All of them; right. So he was well-known in the cafes of the area then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the way up until the time -- I don't know exactly when he went to Austria before the war or when he would not be in jail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew him. Did you like him before the war, when he came to your cafes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had some mutual friends. There was Miroslav and some others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would this be right, that he was someone who mixed across the ethnic boundaries quite a lot, mixed with Serbs, mixed with Croats, mixed with Muslims quite happily and freely; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He mixed with everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of the people who were in the camp with you, no doubt they also knew him from before the war; would that be right? Would that be something you knew about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've told the court that he had, as you have described it -- everybody respected him. Would this be right, Mr. Dordic, that in the context of what was happening at the camp, that was a respect that he had to earn from the people in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not so much respecting him as that they feared him, because he was their superior. They all looked at him as commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but the word that you used was "respect"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what appeared to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I didn't say that there was respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe it was wrong interpretation there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the word that was translated to us, Mr. Dordic. May I suggest some reasons why that would be so --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were being mistreated by a man called Salko -- do you remember telling us about that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Salko. Salko did not mistreat me ever, but when Zenga burnt my tongue, Salko stood at the door and at one point he said: "Here's Pavo", and then he ran out and told me to get back to my place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they got you quickly back to your place, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I went back by myself, on my own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before Pavo came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He never came. I don't know if that was Salko's trick so that Zenga would leave me alone or something. I don't know. I'm not clear about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was, I think, another occasion when your brother was being assaulted, but you weren't present, I think, at that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you remember hearing from your brother about him being assaulted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was brought out by Kemal Mr.dzic and by -- we called him Crni. He said he was from the Doboj area. We heard they started beating him. We heard the noise of a vehicle and a door opened all of a sudden and he ran inside. After a while they asked Zaro to come out, because Zaro at that time was some kind of a leader. He was sort of superior of us. He was a prisoner but he was appointed our superior. Then when he came out, he said that: "Pavo was asking whether you had been beaten", and Rajko said that he was not, because he didn't dare say "Yes", because again they heard something, and then Zaro apparently went out and told Pavo that he had not been beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But isn't this right, that during the course of your brother being beaten up someone said that Pavo's car was coming; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could even hear the sound of the vehicle. I don't know if that was Pavo's car. That I don't know. We inside heard a car approaching.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But nevertheless, when the car started to approach, the guards took instant steps to conceal both themselves and your brother, so that if it was Pavo, he wouldn't see what was going on; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Me? My brother?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if they hid. I know that my brother came inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't this the case, that that was frequently how matters would happen? If Pavo appeared on the scene, things that were being done wrong would stop, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if something was going on at the time yes, of course it would stop, at least what I know about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now to ask about your transfer to the Musala camp on 21st August. Do you remember that taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the reasons for that was that you were at that time suffering from a skin disease known as psoriasis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because of psoriasis and I was very thin. I was like a skeleton, a walking skeleton.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you will see that I can't share with you the condition of being thin, Mr. Dordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can share with you the experience of having psoriasis. I know a little bit about that. Was your psoriasis very bad at that time? I think you described it as being on your face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on my face, my hands, my body, all over my body, wherever the bones are, all over. I was all covered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- there are a number of ways in which it can manifest itself. Was it just scaling of the skin, dead skin coming off, or was it worse than that? Was there any bleeding from the psoriasis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. As we were perspiring a lot it was very hot, it would scale and then the skin would be very red underneath. The white skin would come off and beneath the skin would be raw red.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Pavo came to see you, it would obviously have been quite obvious to you that you were suffering from that, because your face would show it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me what it was. He didn't know what it was, so I explained it to him. I told him it was psoriasis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just help me about this. Have you always suffered from psoriasis? Have you had it before the war at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 1975. It would appear occasionally, but I always have it here on my elbows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it tends to disappear when you're in the sun and you look as though you've been in the sun a fair bit, Mr. Dordic, recently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes it disappears; sometimes not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he saw you in that condition, he took steps to have you removed to Musala for albeit a short period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, since I was moved, that was probably the reason, and he had the power to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally this, Mr. Dordic, if I may, please: he was responsible for transferring out of the camp Esad Landzo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was him. I think -- the guards told us that it was Pavo who chased him away. I'm not sure, but that was what we heard from the guards. Whether they were lying or not I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whenever it may have happened, the immediate reason for it was that he'd fired a weapon near to some people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He would fire at us. We would hear the firing when we had visits along the wire fence. Whether that was the main reason I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dordic. I have no further questions for you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. Cross-examination by MS. RESIDOVIC MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, if I can have a minute to set myself up, because it's a bit more complicated for us, as we have to find our interpretation booth for Serbo-Croatian or rather the three languages that we now speak. May I start, your Honours? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you have the witness. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Good afternoon, Mr. Dordic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic. I am defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm glad to meet you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been answering for some time questions put to you by my learned colleagues, both the prosecution and the defence, and I have now been asked by the Registry, though I wanted to do that for our own benefit anyway, that we come to an agreement, namely when somebody is putting questions to you in English, then it is normal for you to wait for the interpretation and then to answer the question. However, as both of us speak a language that we understand very well, we get carried away and we enter into a dialogue. So I would like to ask you when you hear my question to wait a bit for the answer until you have heard the question having been interpreted into English and French, and I will do the same, so that everyone is the courtroom will be able to understand what we are talking about. Have I made myself clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dordic, you stated in the Tribunal that around 19th April you left Konjic and went to Bradina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was in Bradina all the time, only I was living in Konjic -- I was working in Konjic until the 19th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were working at the Konjic motel; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the 19th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the 19th. At that time very major disturbances had started in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The situation was very tense between Serbs, Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Mostar the combat operations had already started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as we were informed by the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Sarajevo the conflict started on April 6th; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as we learned by the mass media, because I didn't travel there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also you were informed by the media that on this day a state of -- immediate state of war had been proclaimed in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already stated in your testimony so far that in Bradina, like the rest of the population, because of the fear that was mounting among the people, you yourself tried to organise yourself in the event that you had to defend yourself; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that this was done by other inhabitants of Bradina as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go back to your occupation. You said that you were a waiter and you completed the appropriate training in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you told my colleague that acting as a waiter in many places in Konjic you met many people in Konjic. Some of them you knew by sight and others became acquaintances; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, you were known as "Mrkela"; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just before the war, yes, because of Mrkela, the football player, and I was a Red Star supporter, a supporter of the Red Star team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So some people who were talking about Mrkela the waiter meant you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, I am sure you can confirm in the area of Konjic and especially Bradina the Dordic family is a very large one; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not very large, but among the larger ones in Bradina, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father's name is Nedeljko, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your mother's name, Todora?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And her maiden name was Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Mrkajic family is numerous in Bradina too, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife's maiden name is Mrkajic too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, you are related to this family both by your mother and through your wife; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, Bradina at the time was a component part of the municipality of Konjic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Konjic at the time members of all ethnic groups were living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Muslim population was somewhat more numerous, but everyone was living together; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The municipality has its legal bodies, the Assembly, its committees, the MUP and others; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April, while you were still working, you know that Djuro Kuljanin was the Vice President of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The President was Dr. Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djuro Kuljanin is a Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djuro Kuljanin was never dismissed from his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Until he left. I was not involved in politics but I think they were virtually separated, just before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, you don't know that he was replaced. You know that he came to Bradina, though, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not aware that he came to Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not aware that he was replaced either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Dordic, you told the court that within the framework of your self-organisation you formed guard duty on the road in Bradina, checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Members of the reserve police set up checkpoints. Those who were reserve policemen, and when the reserve police force withdrew -- I don't remember exactly when -- they retreated to Podorasac from Bradina -- then just those who were left from the reserve force controlled the checkpoints from April onwards, let's say from 20th April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, from April 20th in front of Mico's cafe on the main road in Bradina there was a checkpoint held by the local people of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a mistake. Not in front of Mico's cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me where.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the butcher's shop owned by Edo. I don't remember his surname and at the Ivan tunnel, in front of the Ivan tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That checkpoint was not put up by the Konjic authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons who set up the checkpoints had no permission from the executive board of the municipality, nor from any other competent authority. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but at that time there were no people passing through Bradina any more. There were very few people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those who were passed -- allowed to pass at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the checkpoint. I think that had to do with Ilija and down there in Podorasac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, because you were in Konjic until April 19th you know that a general mobilisation had been proclaimed in Konjic on April 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I received a call-up call, which I rejected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, you did not respond to the draft which you received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the kind of call-up call that I received, because it was stated --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that refusal to respond to mobilisation according to the law of our country, both the former Yugoslavia and since, is a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not wish to respond to the call-up in the way it was stated. It asked us to remove the old insignia from uniforms, if we had any uniforms, that they would give us new insignia, and that we should get our own weapons. I did go where we were told to go, to the local community premises, but there was nobody there from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only thing you did was to illegally get yourself a weapon; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, you did -- you were not fired from the motel where you worked the day you went off to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The acting general manager at that time, Marko Draganic, told me: "You're going on unpaid leave."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that leave, you didn't go back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. My documents are still there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope you will be able to go back to work soon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, you testified in court that around 12th or 13th May the first attack occurred in the region of your village, which you successfully repulsed; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't take part in that. That was on the other side, because Bradina covers an area of some 6 to 7 km. as the crow flies. At least it was far away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the defenders who were there, they managed to reject the attack. You know that your neighbour Zovko Zvonko was in charge of that first attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And some people from Repovci -- who was an active duty officer. I can't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But after that you started to arm with greater haste, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. After that we couldn't move anywhere. We simply used the road that is 5 km. long between one tunnel and the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you started digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, not a metre of trenches had been dug out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if your compatriots, the people from your town, said so, then it is wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I at least don't know that they were being dug out and I did not participate in any trench digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, are you aware that the authorities from Konjic had tried through various negotiations to resolve the problem of checkpoints and weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I would hear from them when they came back from these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that they asked -- that they addressed almost an ultimatum that the weapons be handed in and that the road be freed for circulation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the information we were given on 25th, negotiations were to have been held in Podorasac or Bradina -- I'm not sure of that, of the place -- at about noon or 1 o'clock. Agreement was supposed to have been reached to hand over weapons and that we were to be allowed peacefully to cross over into territory held by the Serbs. At least that was the information I received. However, instead of any such agreement an attack ensued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that. However, as you have already testified, neither you nor the other people of Bradina did not hand in your weapons until May 25th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these two checkpoints were not removed by that date, the one in front of the butcher's and the other one in front of the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that you, like others, can testify before this court that virtually anywhere or anywhere along a highway, if checkpoints and barricades are put up, then communication between Konjic and Sarajevo is virtually impossible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that, but barricades were there long ago, so that our barricades were not necessary at all. There were no people passing through Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to go back to your earlier answer, you confirmed a moment ago that some barricades were put up by the legal authorities because of the immediate threat of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On 19th or 20th, the last time I went to Konjic, I saw the checkpoint in Podorasac. This was 20th April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Your brother is Rajko Dordic, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was working in the Territorial Defence staff of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother Rajko was not dismissed from the staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that. He left of his own accord.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly at the same time as you, around April 20th, he came to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was the one to bring him back, because at that time he didn't have a car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you and your brother Rajko went from Konjic to Bradina that day by car and you didn't go back until the period of combat operations that you have discussed here at length?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't go back. That was the last time I left -- I went from there. Only when I was arrested I was taken there by force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the work he had in the Territorial Defence staff, he had some experience in terms of the self-defence of people; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, but there was no organisation really at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless with his knowledge, he assisted people who asked him for his advice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he took part in the work of the crisis staff that was formed in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking before this Tribunal, Mr. Dordic, you recognised on one of the photographs the type of weapon that you had. It is an automatic rifle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I have no understanding of weapons, even though I have seen the picture, I would like to ask you whether it is a rifle that we tend to call popularly a Kalasnikov?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Muslims called it the gypsy, because it was manufactured in Kragoviz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore your rifle was of domestic make?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, you said that you purchased that gun on the black market. Can you tell me whether you local people in Bradina helped each other to find weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who did helped each other, but -- who had secret connections, but they carried their secret to their graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you got your rifle from Branislav Gligorevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He brought it to me and I gave him the money, as much as he asked, and everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also received from Branislav Gligorevic 80 bullets, which you did not use during the operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I got some more later on, so I had a total of some 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are acquainted with Relja Gligorevic, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you help him to get a semi-automatic rifle with 150 bullets through those same channels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, through Branislav Gligorevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dordic, you also know Milivoj Gligorevic, who was a driver in the railways, Sarajevo Railway Company. As he had more money, he helped him to get an automatic rifle and 270 bullets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Ms Residovic, how many longer are you prepared to carry on. If you are concluding, okay. I just want to know how much longer. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. President, I need quite a bit of time yet. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: We are at 5.30 now and we are not likely to sit tomorrow. We are not likely to. The next you can come is Monday at about 11 o'clock. So I don't know. I don't think you can pursue this line of cross-examination now. I didn't think you would take so long a time, but you have your own ideas. I think we will rise now and reassemble on Monday at 11. (5.30 pm)
